notes.claim: The law of cosines says the square of any side of a triangle equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides minus twice their product and the cosine of the included angle.
The cosine rule can be remembered as the Pythagoras theorem with something extra so that it works for all triangles.
The cosine rule finds a missing side or angle when two sides and the included angle, or all three sides, are known.
The sine rule finds a side from another side and two angles, or an angle from two sides and a non-included angle.
With the sine rule the second possible angle is found by subtracting the first answer from 180 degrees, and exists only if the angle sum of the triangle stays within 180 degrees.

The sine rule: side a divided by the sine of angle A equals side b divided by the sine of angle B and side c divided by the sine of angle C (added in i4's review fixes, for the sine rule's general form).
